nodes.label: Cost-Efficient LLM Bakeoff for Agentic Coding
nodes.author: Suhaas Surapaneni
nodes.rationale: Business-facing plan doc: selects a lower-cost Bedrock model to replace Claude Sonnet 5 for agentic coding at Pindrop. Recommends a ~2-2.5 week internal bakeoff because no public benchmark cleanly covers all three candidates.

nodes.label: Kimi K2.5
nodes.rationale: Candidate arm. Leads on the vendor-reported SWE-bench Verified (76.8%) and on AA indices, but the one independent test (Terminal-Bench Hard, 34.8%) puts it below Gemma -- treated as a hypothesis, not a fact. 16K output ceiling risks truncation on large diffs; modified-MIT license needs legal sign-off. Saves only ~80-82%.

nodes.label: Nemotron 3 Super 120B
nodes.rationale: Candidate arm at $0.15/$0.65 with the largest output ceiling (32K). NVIDIA is the only vendor here disclosing multiple harness variants (53.7-60.5%) rather than one cherry-picked number, which is treated as a credibility signal despite the weakest headline score.

nodes.label: Gemma 4 31B
nodes.rationale: Cheapest candidate ($0.14/$0.40, ~96% savings), cleanest license (Apache 2.0), and leader among candidates on both independent benchmarks that cover it. No SWE-bench Verified score exists at all, and it is newest on Bedrock (June 2026) via the bedrock-mantle endpoint, so it carries the least production history.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 5 (incumbent reference)
nodes.rationale: The incumbent, priced $3.00/$15.00 standard tier and used as the $5,000/month cost baseline. Artificial Analysis found its cost per completed task runs ~15% above Opus 4.8 despite a lower per-token price, which is the evidence for deciding on cost per completed workflow rather than per token.

nodes.label: Self-hosted LiteLLM proxy as the access layer
nodes.rationale: One unified way to call and switch between all candidate models with built-in cost tracking, running inside Pindrop's own AWS account so no data passes through a third party.

nodes.label: OpenRouter rejected as routing layer
nodes.rationale: Even under Bring-Your-Own-Key, requests still transit OpenRouter's own servers before reaching Bedrock and carry a ~5% fee -- which cuts against the pricing and data-residency reasons Pindrop standardized on Bedrock in the first place.

nodes.label: SWE-bench Verified (contamination caveat)
nodes.rationale: Included because it is the only benchmark with real coverage, not because it is trustworthy: OpenAI stopped reporting it in Feb 2026 after an audit of 138 tasks found ~59% materially flawed and every frontier model tested had memorized the human-written fix.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench Hard (independent agentic CLI)
nodes.rationale: The only independently-run benchmark covering two of the three candidates; its disagreement with vendor numbers (Kimi 34.8% independent vs 50.8% vendor on a different track) is the direct evidence that vendor claims cannot decide this.

nodes.label: Artificial Analysis Index scores
nodes.rationale: Independent composite (Intelligence Index, Coding Index, output speed) kept in its own table rather than mixed with task-specific benchmarks, because it is a different lens and blending the two would imply comparability that does not exist.

nodes.label: Cost per completed workflow
nodes.rationale: The decision metric, not cost per token: a model that burns tokens or retries to reach the same answer is not cheap. Grounded in AA's measurement that Sonnet 5 costs ~15% more per completed task than Opus 4.8 at a lower per-token price.

nodes.label: Two-tier internal eval set (Tier A bug fix / Tier B feature scale)
nodes.rationale: 40-60 tasks on real Pindrop repos, N>=3 samples graded blind. Tier B (multi-file) is where the recommendation is said to be won or lost, because no public benchmark has contamination-clean coverage of all three candidates.

nodes.label: bedrock-mantle endpoint
nodes.rationale: Gemma 4 31B is served here rather than on standard bedrock-runtime, which is why it does not appear under the console's Serverless model-catalog filter and why Phase 0 must confirm the endpoint per model.

nodes.label: Plan-doc success criteria and thresholds
nodes.rationale: Task completion >=90% of Sonnet 5 weighted to Tier B, terminal-command success >=95%, cross-file changes correct >=90%, cost <=40% of Sonnet 5 per completed workflow. The design spec later demotes these from gates to reference points.
